cohort: 598 term primiparous women (296 with cesarean section due to labor dystocia and 302 with vaginal delivery)
finding: Rising maternal pre-pregnancy BMI was strongly associated with labor dystocia risk, with a 10% elevated risk of CS for every 1 kg/m2 increase in BMI.
mod_finding: Rising maternal pre-pregnancy BMI was strongly associated with an increased risk of cesarean section due to labor dystocia.
